Thin-Crust Pizza Dough

This stiffer dough rolls thin. Dock it with a fork if a bubble would lift the toppings. Roll 4 thin rounds of 200 g each. Add another round by raising the ball count.

Detailed method

Thin-crust pizzas. Currently 508.3 g flour, 55% hydration, 0% starter, 2% salt, and 0.4% yeast. That is 279.5 g water, 10.2 g salt, and 2 g yeast, 800 g of dough. Currently 4 pizzas of 200 g each. Sauce, cheese, and other toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 508.3 g flour, 279.5 g water, 10.2 g salt, and 2 g instant yeast until no dry flour remains, then knead 6 to 8 minutes until smooth. At 55% the dough is firm. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 45 to 75 minutes. With 0.4% yeast it should grow by about half.
  3. Roll Divide the 800 g into 4 pieces of 200 g each. Rest each piece 15 minutes, roll it thin with a pin, about 3 mm, and dock it with a fork. The default 800 g uses a baking stone or tray about 40 cm across. If you change the amount, use a stone sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  4. Top Add sauce and cheese if you want them. Those toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. Keep the layer thin so the center stays crisp.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a stone or steel for 30 minutes. Bake 8 to 12 minutes, until the rim is spotted and the center is dry. Rest 2 minutes before you cut.
